highlightAliases.old: Components of the Geriatric Assessment In addition to the standard medical history and physical examination, the clinician should systematically search for specific conditions that are common among older persons and that might have considerable impact on function.
highlightAliases.new: Components of the Geriatric Assessment

highlightAliases.old: Visual Impairment Visual impairment is a common and often underreported problem in the older population.
highlightAliases.new: Visual impairment is a common and often underreported problem in the older population.

highlightAliases.old: Hearing Impairment Hearing impairment is among the most common medical conditions reported by older persons, affecting approximately one-third of those age 65 or older.
highlightAliases.new: Hearing impairment is among the most common medical conditions reported by older persons, affecting approximately one-third of those age 65 or older.

highlightAliases.old: Malnutrition/Weight Loss (See Also Chapter 30) Malnutrition is a global term that encompasses many different nutritional problems that are associated with diverse health consequences.
highlightAliases.new: Malnutrition is a global term that encompasses many different nutritional problems that are associated with diverse health consequences.

highlightAliases.old: Urinary Incontinence Urinary incontinence is common and estimated to affect 11% to 34% of older men and 17% to 55% of older women.
highlightAliases.new: Urinary incontinence is common and estimated to affect 11% to 34% of older men and 17% to 55% of older women.

highlightAliases.old: Balance and Gait Impairments and Falling Over one-third of community-dwelling persons older than 65 fall every year.
highlightAliases.new: Over one-third of community-dwelling persons older than 65 fall every year.

highlightAliases.old: Polypharmacy (See Also Chapter 22) Polypharmacy in older patients is associated with adverse drug reactions, reduced adherence, and inappropriate medication usage.
highlightAliases.new: Polypharmacy in older patients is associated with adverse drug reactions, reduced adherence, and inappropriate medication usage.

highlightAliases.old: Affective Assessment (See Also Chapter 65) Major depression and other affective disorders are common among the older persons and are likely underdiagnosed owing to underreported symptoms, atypical presentations, or comorbid cognitive impairment or other neurologic diseases such as Parkinson disease.
highlightAliases.new: Major depression and other affective disorders are common among the older persons and are likely underdiagnosed owing to underreported symptoms, atypical presentations, or comorbid cognitive impairment or other neurologic diseases such as Parkinson disease.

highlightAliases.old: Assessment of Function Measurement of functional status is an essential component of the assessment of older persons.
highlightAliases.new: Measurement of functional status is an essential component of the assessment of older persons.

highlightAliases.old: Frailty Frailty is a clinical syndrome where dysregulation of multiple physiologic systems reaches a critical threshold which results in a physiologic state of heightened vulnerability.
highlightAliases.new: Frailty is a clinical syndrome where dysregulation of multiple physiologic systems reaches a critical threshold which results in a physiologic state of heightened vulnerability.

highlightAliases.old: Assessment of Social Support The composition of the older patient’s social support structure can be assessed by asking about their relationships, such as with family, friends, neighbors, and caregivers, as well as the quality of these relationships in the social history.
highlightAliases.new: Assessment of Social Support

highlightAliases.old: Environmental Assessment Environmental assessment encompasses two dimensions, the safety of the home environment and the adequacy of the patient’s access to needed personal and medical services.
highlightAliases.new: Environmental assessment encompasses two dimensions, the safety of the home environment and the adequacy of the patient’s access to needed personal and medical services.

highlightAliases.old: Spirituality Spirituality, whether affiliated with a formal religious denomination or nonreligious intangible elements, has been recognized as an important influence on health and quality of life.
highlightAliases.new: Spirituality, whether affiliated with a formal religious denomination or nonreligious intangible elements, has been recognized as an important influence on health and quality of life.

highlightAliases.old: Goals of Care and Advance Directives Although goals of care and advance directives both solicit patient preferences, they are conceptually different.
highlightAliases.new: Goals of Care and Advance Directives

highlightAliases.old: A Strategic Approach to Geriatric Assessment Much of the information needed to assess older persons can be obtained from old records, other professional or nonprofessional staff, or by self-report from patients or family members completing forms, rather than from direct clinician interview.
highlightAliases.new: A Strategic Approach to Geriatric Assessment

highlightAliases.old: Components of Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment The process of care rendered by CGA teams can be divided into six key elements: (1) data gathering; (2) discussion among the team; (3) development of a treatment plan; (4) implementation of the treatment plan; (5) monitoring response to the treatment plan; and (6) revising the treatment plan.
highlightAliases.new: The process of care rendered by CGA teams can be divided into six key elements: (1) data gathering; (2) discussion among the team; (3) development of a treatment plan; (4) implementation of the treatment plan; (5) monitoring response to the treatment plan; and (6) revising the treatment plan.

highlightAliases.old: Effectiveness of Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment In virtually all studies of CGA, the process has resulted in improved detection and documentation of geriatric problems.
highlightAliases.new: In virtually all studies of CGA, the process has resulted in improved detection and documentation of geriatric problems.

highlightAliases.old: Inpatient Units and Services Geriatric Evaluation and Management Units (GEMUs), also referred to as Acute Care of the Elderly (ACE) units, are designed to be environment friendly to older persons.
highlightAliases.new: Inpatient Units and Services

highlightAliases.old: Posthospital Discharge Assessment and Management Studies of CGA have found inconsistent benefits for posthospital discharge programs.
highlightAliases.new: Posthospital Discharge Assessment and Management

highlightAliases.old: Outpatient CGA The evidence for outpatient CGA has been inconsistent.
highlightAliases.new: The evidence for outpatient CGA has been inconsistent.

highlightAliases.old: Lessons Learned From Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment Despite unresolved issues regarding the effectiveness of CGA, the principles of CGA have been incorporated into a number of programs that have been demonstrated to be effective.
highlightAliases.new: Lessons Learned From Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment
